description: HELD-OUT synthetic benign-hard-negative corpus. Authored in a separate pass and hash-pinned BEFORE any detector change in the P15b hard-negative work, so the fix could not be tuned against it. Covers the injection-ADJACENT constructions that a real deployment sees constantly: 'ignore the previous <not-instructions>', the attack phrase quoted as the object of a translate/explain/test request, security documentation about prompt injection, ordinary developer traffic, and business text that mentions rules or instructions innocuously. It ALSO carries six genuine attacks — a benign-only corpus would be satisfied by switching the detector off, so recall has to survive the false-positive fix. SYNTHETIC: a generalisation check on hand-authored data, NOT evidence of real-world false-positive rates. EXT-EFFICACY remains open.

labeling_protocol.adjudication: none — single author, no second opinion
labeling_protocol.method: authored-with-intent, held out: written to be examples of their declared labels and hash-pinned before the detector change, so labels could not drift to match an outcome. Ground truth is the author's intent, not an observation.

provenance.authorization: none required — contains no customer, tenant, or personal data
